items.title: debugging.md S2 (`dbg_stack()`) prerequisite: the resource move scan records no per-site state, so an expansion cannot know that a binding is moved (or moved on some paths) at the `dbg_stack()` site without reading it — and a read there is refused as R1
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order48/debug-48/finds/s2_prerequisites.vl` (vilan 0.45.0 + debug-48). `guard` is consumed at 29:10; a read of `guard` at the marked site is refused (`use of \`guard\` after it was moved`), and `dbg_stack()` must instead print `guard: Guard = <moved at 29:10>` (or `<moved on some paths>`, R7's state). `check_resource_moves` (`scan_bodies_for_moves` over `MoveFlow`) holds exactly this state while it scans and throws it away; it records violations only. What S2 needs: at a call the analyzer marked as `dbg_stack()`, the scan records `MoveFlow.moved` (binding -> move site) and the conditional-move set, keyed by the call, on the `Program`. The pass slot exists: an expansion pass between `check_resource_moves` and `liveness::LastUse::compute` (both in the analysis driver) would see those verdicts and still have its minted `Ref` reads counted by liveness and drop planning. Owner of the scan: solver (checks). debug-48 stopped S2 on this and the view twin (R-d).

items.title: debugging.md S2 (`dbg_stack()`) prerequisite: the view-invalidation scan records no per-site state, so an expansion cannot know that a match-capture view past its last use was invalidated by a push — and reading it at the `dbg_stack()` site makes the push a rule-4 error
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order48/debug-48/finds/s2_prerequisites.vl`. `first` is a match-capture view into `rows` (B509 Q3: it leaves the live set at its last use), then `rows.push(None)` at 34:4 is accepted. A read of `*first` at the marked site is refused (`cannot mutate 'rows' with '.push(..)' while a view into it is live`), because the read extends the view's life over the push. `dbg_stack()` must print `first: view i32 = <view, invalidated by push at 34:4>` without reading it. Under the lexical rule 4 this is the only way a view in scope can be invalid at a point (a `let` view is refused at the push itself), so the verdict needed is narrow: `check_invalidation`'s scan (`scan_invalidation`, `InvalidationScanState.capture_uses`) records, at a `dbg_stack()` call, which capture views have left the live set and which event since touched their root. Owner: solver (checks). debug-48 stopped S2 on this and the move twin (R-d).

items.title: A fixed-array literal under a `[T; n]` annotation is emitted natively as `vec![..]` while the binding's type renders `[i32; 3]`: `let fixed: [i32; 3] = [1, 2, 3]; first(fixed)` is refused by rustc (E0308, expected `[i32; 3]`, found `Vec<i32>`)

`Debug` still misses types `dbg` prints: `[derive(Debug)]` over a `HashMap`, `HashSet`, `Shared`, `SignalCell`, `BigInt`, fixed-array `[T; n]` or closure field fails inside the generated code ("HashMap<str, i32> has no method 'debug'"), and `T: Debug` refuses them
items.body: Repros: `sweeps/order48/debug-48/finds/debug_derive_over_handles.vl` (a struct with `HashMap<str, i32>`, `Shared<i32>` and `BigInt` fields: three errors 'in code generated by this attribute: … has no method debug') and `debug_derive_over_array_and_closure.vl` (`[i32; 2]`, `\|i32\| i32`). `dbg` prints every one of them (`HashMap { "a" => 1 }`, `Shared(1)`, `[1, 2]`, `<closure \|i32\| i32>`), so E275's rule that a derived `.debug()` is `dbg`'s spelling on one line has holes exactly here. debugging.md §2.2 asks std to ship `Debug` impls for its handle types; S4 shipped `List`, `Option` and `Result` only (tuples wait on B557, E260). Rec: impls in std beside each type (`hash_map.vl`, `hash_set.vl`, `shared.vl`, the cell, `bigint`) spelled as the printer spells them, plus `[T; n]` beside `List`; a closure field keeps refusing (or the derive writes the printer's `<closure ..>` text). Not built in debug-48: `debug.vl` is one of the modules a macro world force-loads, so adding imports there needs the world's load set checked first. Found by debug-48 probing E275.
